samples: This module represents arithmetic expressions (decimal numbers, addition, multiplication, and negation) as a tree. It provides one function that computes the expression's value and another that renders it as fully parenthesized infix text. Its main function builds one hard-coded sample expression and prints it with its result to the console, so it works as a small demonstration or a base for a larger evaluator rather than a tool that reads user input.

This module models arithmetic expressions as a tree of numbers, additions, multiplications and negations over decimals. It offers one function that computes an expression's value and another that prints it in fully parenthesized infix form. Its main function builds a small sample expression and prints it alongside its result, so it is a clear, self-contained demo or starting point rather than a parser or full calculator.

This module defines a tree representation of arithmetic expressions (decimal numbers, addition, multiplication, and negation) along with two pure functions: one that computes an expression's value and one that renders it as fully parenthesized infix text. Its `main` function builds a small sample expression and prints the rendered form together with its computed value to the console, so it works as a demonstration of the pattern rather than a tool that parses or accepts user input. It needs only console access and has no other side effects, which makes it safe to reuse as a small library for evaluating or displaying expression trees you construct in code.

This module models arithmetic expressions as a tree of decimal numbers, addition, multiplication and negation. It provides one function that computes an expression's value and another that renders it as fully parenthesized infix text. Its main function builds one small sample expression and prints the rendered text next to the result, so it works as a demo or a base for a calculator, not a parser or a general-purpose tool.

This module models arithmetic expressions as a tree of numbers, additions, multiplications and negations, with one function that computes the decimal value and another that prints it in fully parenthesized infix form. It is pure apart from a demo `main` that builds one sample expression and prints it alongside its result to the console. It is a small, self-contained example, useful as a template for recursive tree handling but not a full parser or calculator, since it has no text input, subtraction or division.
